text:
mike: heads up — starting perf onboarding for Talos-8B on dedicated pool A. primary asks: cold-start latency, sustained qps, batching sweet spots, ctx=2k/8k sweep, and int8 vs fp16 throughput.

anya: sounds good. can we prioritize cold-start + kv-warmup behavior first? our customers see big p95 hits after scale-to-zero.

ravi: agreed. plan: 1) cold-start tracer (measure model load, jitted kernels, mmap) 2) kv-cache warmup probe (inject repeated prefixes) 3) microbench for small/medium/large batches.

kevin: add these to checklist: env: GPU driver 535.86, CUDA 12.1, cudnn 9.x. quant builds: LLMINT8 and NNQ-approx. tag images as talos8b:fp16 and talos8b:int8.

mike: +1. I'll allocate 2 nodes (A1,A2) with 4xH100 each. scheduling note: avoid colocated heavy workloads during tests.

anya: prompt set for throughput should include: short prompts (10 tokens), convo-medium (60 tokens), long-prefill (512 tokens). for quality/regression: use our eval set talos-qual-2026 (500 prompts).

ravi: quick command for the cold-start tracer:

```
perf-run --image=talos8b:fp16 --node=A1 --trace=load,mmap,kernels --out=/tmp/talos-cold.json
```

mike: perf-bot will post results when runs finish.

perf-bot: run queued: talos8b-cold-A1 (id=run-4892). estimated 12m.

anya: for batching sweep let's define batch sizes [1,2,4,8,16,32] and sequence lengths [32,128,512,2048]. record latency distribution (p50,p90,p95,p99) and tokens/sec.

kevin: note: when using int8, ensure we test two kernel variants (fast-gemm vs fallback) and collect GPU utilization + SM occupancy. put nvprof logs in run metadata.

ravi: for ctx sweep: use synthetic prefix to saturate kv cache. measure incremental token latency as ctx grows. expect memory-bound at 8k. watch for kernel fallback at >6k.

mike: scheduling a smoke run at 09:00 UTC tomorrow, then full sweep mid-day. anyone object?

anya: no objections. I'll own quality evals and prompt set. I'll also run a baseline fp16 pass for comparison.

kevin: I'll prepare the int8 build and docker tags. also add deployment test to verify zero-downtime fallback to smaller batch sizes.

perf-bot: run started: run-4892 (talos8b-cold-A1).

ravi: when logging results, include these keys in the JSON: run_id, image_tag, node, batch_size, seq_len, p50, p90, p95, p99, tokens_per_sec, gpu_util, mem_alloc, kernel_fallbacks, notes. keeps eval tooling compatible.

anya: reminder: include quality checkpoints after quantization. run talos-qual-2026 on the int8 candidate and save score diffs vs fp16. set alert if macro-bleu drops >1.5 or hallucination-rate increases >2%.

mike: perfect. I'll post the smoke run logs here once perf-bot uploads.

perf-bot: run completed: run-4892. summary: cold-load 18.2s, mmap 4.0s, kernel-jit 3.1s, total p95 26.0s. artifact: https://internal.storage/runs/run-4892/talos-cold.json

anya: 18s cold-start is within our current SLO for dedicated nodes but still heavy. can we prefetch weights via mmap warmup during scaling events?

kevin: we can add a pre-warm hook to the autoscaler: when new pod scheduled, kick a lightweight mmap touch + one priming token. I'll prototype.

ravi: next steps: run full batching sweep fp16 on A1, int8 on A2, then ctx sweep on A1. collect summaries and nominate a candidate for internal preview.

mike: assigned: anya (quality), kevin (int8 build/ops), ravi (bench harness), mike (orchestration). update this thread with artifacts and short summary (1-2 lines) per run. :thumbsup:
